# Recurring Giving Explained: A Practical Guide for Sustainable Nonprofit Revenue


Print


#### [Giving](https://blackbaudgivingfund.org/blog/category/giving/) ,[Strategy](https://blackbaudgivingfund.org/blog/category/strategy/) ,[Workplace Giving](https://blackbaudgivingfund.org/blog/category/workplace-giving/)


August 31, 2026 | 9 min read By:[Catherine LaCour](https://blackbaudgivingfund.org/blog/authors/catherine-lacour/)


Key Takeaways:


- The different types of recurring giving programs nonprofits should understand.


- How workplace giving can strengthen recurring revenue.


- What donors expect from modern recurring giving experiences.


- How to prepare your nonprofit before promoting recurring giving.


- Practical ways to encourage more supporters to become recurring donors.


- A recurring giving readiness checklist your team can implement today.


The most sustainable fundraising strategies aren’t built on individual transactions. They’re built on ongoing relationships. Recurring giving turns moments of generosity into lasting partnerships, giving donors an easy way to support causes they care about while creating a reliable, year-round revenue source for nonprofits.


That reliability matters in an environment where nonprofit leaders are being asked to plan for the future while facing increasing uncertainty around when funding will arrive and what needs may emerge next. A strong recurring giving program will bring greater consistency, helping fundraisers build a more predictable revenue base, plan with greater confidence, and be ready to act when their communities need them most.


As donor expectations continue to evolve, recurring giving is more than a fundraising tactic. It’s an essential part of a dependable fundraising strategy. When paired with


[workplace giving](https://blackbaudgivingfund.org/blog/what-is-workplace-giving-and-why-its-important-for-nonprofits/) programs, employer matching, and strong donor stewardship, recurring giving helps fundraisers build dependable revenue streams while strengthening relationships with supporters over time.


Recurring revenue helps:


- Stabilize ongoing cash flow and eliminate the guesswork from annual planning.


- Reduce dependence on high-stress year-end fundraising.


- [Increase donor retention and lower fundraising costs](https://www.blackbaud.com/industry-insights/glossary/a-guide-to-recurring-donations-from-one-time-gifts-to-lifelong-supporters) .


- Strengthen long-term donor relationships.


- Create more flexibility to respond quickly when community needs arise.


### Why Recurring Giving Matters More Than Ever


Recurring donors often become the most loyal advocates for a cause, staying connected to your mission throughout the year, often


[giving 600% more](https://www.blackbaud.com/industry-insights/glossary/a-guide-to-recurring-donations-from-one-time-gifts-to-lifelong-supporters) than one-time givers. That ongoing relationship creates more opportunities to share impact, recognize generosity, and strengthen long-term engagement.


Recurring giving also benefits donors. Smaller monthly gifts often feel more manageable than larger one-time contributions, which allows supporters to make a meaningful impact throughout the year.


### Recurring Giving Starts With Donor Trust


Donors are more likely to commit to ongoing support when they feel confident in your organization. That confidence isn’t built through a single annual report or one email outreach. It’s reinforced through consistent communication, transparency, and visible impact throughout the donor journey.


Ask yourself:


- Can supporters quickly find information about my nonprofit online?


- Is it easy to understand our mission?


- Is messaging consistent acrossall the places my nonprofit appears?


- Do donors regularly hear how their gifts are making a difference?


- Is the donation experience simple and secure?


- Do donors receive timely acknowledgments and updates?


Every interaction helps strengthen the trust required for a donor to make a long-term commitment.


### The Different Types of Recurring Giving


Recurring giving can take several forms:


****


- **Monthly Giving Programs:** The most familiar model allows donors to automatically contribute a set amount every month through a donation platform.


- **Payroll Giving:** Many companies allow employees to make charitable donations directly from their paycheck.


- **Workplace Giving Platforms:** Many businesses are enrolled in giving platforms that make recurring payroll deductions simple and connect employees with thousands of vetted nonprofits. These programs often introduce nonprofits to new supporters they might not reach on their own.


- **Employer Matching Gifts:** Recurring gifts can become even more valuable when employers match employee donations, doubling or sometimes tripling the original donation amount.


Employer matching is the single biggest multiplier for recurring gifts, so encourage your supporters to check if their employer offers matching gifts to significantly increase the impact of their donations. Educating donors about recurring giving, workplace giving, and matching opportunities is a vital part of a successful fundraising strategy.


### How Workplace Giving Strengthens Recurring Giving


Fundraisers often overlook workplace giving as an actionable strategy. Over


[26 million employees](https://doublethedonation.com/matching-gift-statistics/) have access to workplace giving programs, so it’s a strategy fundraisers cannot afford to overlook. These programs often include recurring payroll contributions, matching gift programs, volunteer grants, and


[corporate giving initiatives](https://blackbaudgivingfund.org/blog/how-to-build-corporate-partnerships-that-drive-long-term-nonprofit-revenue/) that make it automatic for employees to give.


If your nonprofit is enrolled in workplace giving platforms, you may already be receiving recurring donations without realizing where they originated. Fundraisers that maintain up-to-date profiles in workplace giving platforms, like

This ensures your organization shows up when corporate employees set up their recurring contributions. ### Recurring Giving Readiness Checklist: Are You Ready to Retain Donors?


Before investing your time in recurring giving campaigns, evaluate whether your organization is prepared to steward and keep these supporters long-term.


**Donor Experience**


- Our online donation process is simple and mobile-friendly.


- Recurring giving is prominently featured on our website and donor pages.


- Donors can choose recurring gifts with just a few clicks.


- Donation confirmation emails clearly explain what happens next and show immediate gratitude.


**Stewardship**


- We have a welcome email series specifically for recurring donors.


- We thank recurring donors regularly, not just after the initial gift.


- We provide ongoing impact stories throughout the year to prove their money is working.


- We recognize donor milestones such as one-year anniversaries.


**Workplace Giving Readiness**


- Our nonprofit is registered and verified with workplace giving platforms.


- We educate donors about employer matching opportunities during the sign-up process.


- We remind supporters to check whether their employer matches donations or volunteer hours.


- Our nonprofit profile is current across all giving platforms so we look credible and active.


**Internal Operations**


- We monitor recurring donor retention rates month over month.


- We regularly review recurring gift conversion rates.


- We have a clear, gentle process for reaching out when recurring gifts stop due to expired credit cards.


- Our fundraising team tracks recurring giving alongside other fundraising metrics.


### Five Ways to Turn Supporters Into Lifelong Monthly Backers


Once your team is prepared to receive and steward recurring donations, follow these five steps to recruit new donors to support your nonprofit for the long term:


1. **Show impact throughout the year.** Recurring donors want to know their continued support is making a difference. Share short, real stories instead of long annual reports.


2. **Make enrollment simple** . Reduce unnecessary fields and allow donors to choose recurring giving with one clear click during every donation experience.


3. **Highlight affordability** . Show how a modest monthly gift (like $15 or $25 a month) can create meaningful impact over time without stretching their personal budget.


4. **Promote employer matching** . Encourage donors to see whether their company matches recurring gifts, potentially doubling or tripling their support all year long.


5. **Ask consistently** . Recurring giving shouldn’t appear only during year-end campaigns. Include the option in appeals, newsletters, event follow-ups, volunteer communications, and thank-you emails as the default way to support the mission.


### Building Sustainable Fundraising Starts With Long-Term Relationships


Recurring giving isn’t simply about increasing the number of monthly donors. It’s about creating a fundraising strategy that reflects how the evolving donor gives with confidence.


When fundraisers combine recurring giving with strong stewardship, workplace giving opportunities, employer matching, and transparent communication, they build a dependable financial foundation that outlasts any single campaign.


The nonprofits that invest in these relationships now will create lasting impact for the communities they serve.
